question: Can a prediction of the unmeasured suffix returns reduce reversals in randomized first-write training targets and improve the realized F1 of an evidence-conditioned two-stage controller?
estimator: For a donor with a randomized first-write pivot and observed physical suffix b, form sum_s[pi1s*m1s-pi0s*m0s] + 2*[pi1b*(Y1b-m1b)-pi0b*(Y0b-m0b)]. Retain exactly the previous verified-credit increment 2*min(pi1b,pi0b)*credit_b. The primary m consists of four estimates of mean per-question F1 from fully measured early training windows, conditioned on donor question category and evidence linkage (first/last/both). Shrink each group to four global cell means with eight pseudo-questions. Exclude the target dialogue and the training donor dialogue from terminal propensity fitting and baseline estimation. No target question, evidence, future session or readout enters the write-time policy. Keep the five original evidence-transport arms, native logit, temperature .05 and +/-2 clip.
comparisons: The paired arm centers on a constant .5 and the difficulty arm uses the same fitted stratum difficulty for every cell. Both arms use the same verified terminal actor. A further resolved variant uses all four physically measured donor returns in place of the fitted baseline while keeping exactly the originally assigned verified credit and unchanged terminal actor. Unmeasured credits are not imputed. Preserve native, terminal PPO, underlying raw F1, blind evidence weights, shuffled labels, equal suffix, return-only and matched-rate comparisons.
diagnostic: Use all 12 early training windows / 91 questions, six histories. For single-question training targets, mask either suffix of each real window at the already-frozen pilot terminal propensities, using other histories only for fitting. Then measure effects on an actual policy by using six session-5 windows as complete anchors and six session-7 windows as root-pivot donors. Enumerate all 64 allocations of their fair suffix coins; for each target exclude its complete history, exclude each donor as well for its training continuation and outcome baseline. Compare paired, difficulty, assisted and physically resolved root training on the very same masked donors and held four-path returns. Report question-weighted expected F1, dispersion over assignments, probability movement, and agreement with the actual held root sign. These are diagnostics on training histories.
chronological: Freeze an interim learner using all 91 early questions plus all six session-9 pairs with verified credit (45 questions); forecast all 12 early windows and every session-11+ target. This interim stage is diagnostic. The primary learner uses the 91 early and all 88 randomized donor questions (sessions 9-12) before forecasting the 40 session-13+ windows / 378 questions. The resolved learner uses that same population once all donor-factorial reports are present and verified. Evaluate full and resolved separately against their own frozen matched controls. Require the previous evidence-transport promotion conditions plus positive focal gain over the fixed .5 paired backup. For the resolved variant also report the trained-baseline version on the same paths. Require >=90% coverage, >=4/6 dialogue wins against matched rate, >=.02 focal F1 over native AND terminal, positive against raw, sham, blind and rate, positive joint HT vs native, and positive focal gain vs native in strictly prospective windows. Independent full-history development, locked LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S testing follow the existing gates. No evaluation-set labels enter these learners.
